sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半打给总统，他接了电话。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超赞圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我很喜欢一锅端的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，持续陪伴您理解世界，充分过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅即可享受特别优惠，网址为nytimes.com斜杠subscribe。

sentences.en: This is Daily Producer Caitlin O'Keefe and I'm here with my colleague Anna Foley.
sentences.zh: 我是每日节目制作人凯特琳·奥基夫，我和我的同事安娜·弗利在这里。

sentences.en: Anna, what time is it and where are we?
sentences.zh: 安娜，现在几点，我们在哪里？

sentences.en: It's currently 6.08 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 目前是清晨6点08分。

sentences.en: We are walking up to the State Farm Stadium.
sentences.zh: 我们正走向州农场体育馆。

sentences.en: There's a huge parking lot that is just like mazes full of people waiting in line.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个巨大的停车场，就像迷宫一样挤满了排队的人。

sentences.en: And they're all here for Charlie Kirk's memorial service in Glendale, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 他们都是为了参加在亚利桑那州格兰代尔举行的查理·柯克的追悼会而来的。

sentences.en: And that's why we're here, to talk to them.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们来这里的原因，来和他们聊聊。

sentences.en: The back in the line!
sentences.zh: 回到队伍后面去！

sentences.en: What time did you get here this morning?
sentences.zh: 你们今天早上几点来的？

sentences.en: We woke up at 3.30 and then left at 4.
sentences.zh: 我们3点半醒来，4点出发。

sentences.en: We got up at 2.30 this morning and showed up here around 4.10.
sentences.zh: 我们今天早上2点半起床，4点10分左右到这儿。

sentences.en: Me and my friend drove 16 hours straight from East Texas and have not slept one wink.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友从德州东部连续开了16个小时的车，一眼都没合过。

sentences.en: If you could say in one or two words how you're feeling right now, what would you say?
sentences.zh: 如果你能用一两个词形容你现在的感受，你会说什么？

sentences.en: Heartbroken.
sentences.zh: 心碎。

sentences.en: Shocked.
sentences.zh: 震惊。

sentences.en: I'm feeling moved by the movement.
sentences.zh: 我为这场运动感到触动。

sentences.en: Probably empowered, definitely.
sentences.zh: 可能感到充满力量，绝对是的。

sentences.en: I think everybody here feels like we lost a leader and truly, honestly, one of God's soldiers.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这里的每个人都觉得我们失去了领袖，真心实意地，他是上帝的战士之一。

sentences.en: It really feels like they killed one of ours.
sentences.zh: 真的感觉他们杀了我们自己人。

sentences.en: What made you decide to come out today?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你决定今天出来的？

sentences.en: This is a historical moment.
sentences.zh: 这是历史性的时刻。

sentences.en: This was a Martin Luther King Jr.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们这个时代的小马丁·路德·金

sentences.en: in our day that was essentially assassinated for his free speech.
sentences.zh: 因为他的言论自由而基本上遭到了暗杀。

sentences.en: And this is our turning point as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们的转折点。

sentences.en: I think this is igniting a fire in America.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正在点燃美国的一把火。

sentences.en: There is a sense of good and evil.
sentences.zh: 有一种正义与邪恶之分。

sentences.en: There is a sense of right and wrong.
sentences.zh: 有一种正确与错误之分。

sentences.en: And this is kind of the time people are waking up to realize, which side am I going to be on?
sentences.zh: 现在正是人们开始清醒并意识到我要站在哪一边的时候。

sentences.en: They wanted to silence him and they turned him into a martyr.
sentences.zh: 他们想要让他闭嘴，却把他变成了一位烈士。

sentences.en: What do you hope to hear in there?
sentences.zh: 你希望在里面听到什么？

sentences.en: I want to hear true leadership say that they will no longer tolerate this.
sentences.zh: 我想听到真正的领袖说他们绝不再容忍这种事。

sentences.en: Not with words, but with policies, with laws.
sentences.zh: 不是用言语，而是用政策，用法律。

sentences.en: No longer being tolerant to the left.
sentences.zh: 不再对左翼保持宽容。

sentences.en: It's now clear that the one person that was willing to reach across the aisle and have conversations with them, they shot him.
sentences.zh: 现在很明显，那个愿意跨越党派界限与他们对话的人，被他们枪杀鸟。

sentences.en: So at this point, there is no changing their minds.
sentences.zh: 所以到了这个地步，他们的想法是无法改变的。

sentences.en: There is no kumbaya anymore.
sentences.zh: 再也没有什么大团圆了。

sentences.en: You're over there.
sentences.zh: 你们在那边。

sentences.en: We're over here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这边。

sentences.en: You stand for that.
sentences.zh: 你们支持那个。

sentences.en: We stand for this.
sentences.zh: 我们支持这个。

sentences.en: Why is it always our side being attacked?
sentences.zh: 为什么总是我们这一方遭到攻击？

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日》节目。

sentences.en: On Sunday, conservatives from all around the country flocked to Arizona to memorialize the slain political leader, Charlie Kirk.
sentences.zh: 周日，来自全国各地的保守派涌向亚利桑那州，悼念遇害的政治领袖查理·柯克。

sentences.en: The service included leaders from the highest levels of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 追悼会出席者包括美国政府最高层的领导人

sentences.en: government, including Vice President Vance and President Trump.
sentences.zh: 包括万斯副总统和特朗普总统。

sentences.en: During the memorial, two clear messages emerged.
sentences.zh: 在追悼会期间，两个清晰的信息浮现出来。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Robert Draper explains how the collision of those two messages makes this a crucial moment for the MAGA movement.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事罗伯特·德雷珀解释了这两种信息的碰撞如何使这成为MAGA运动的关键时刻。

sentences.en: Robert, thank you so much for being here.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，非常感谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: It's been such a long day for you.
sentences.zh: 对你来说这真是漫长的一天。

sentences.en: I can't even imagine what time you had to wake up this morning to cover the funeral.
sentences.zh: 我甚至无法想象你今天早上为了报道这场葬礼几点就得醒来。

sentences.en: I think it was 3.20 a.m., but in any event, I'm happy to be speaking to you.
sentences.zh: 我想是凌晨3点20分，但无论如何，我很高兴能和你交谈。

sentences.en: So you were out reporting in the crowd all day today at Charlie Kirk's memorial service, and I wonder if you could just start by describing what the scene was like.
sentences.zh: 所以你今天一整天都在查理·柯克的追悼会上在人群中进行报道，我想请你先描述一下现场是什么样子的。

sentences.en: Well, it certainly met, if not exceeded, Turning Point USA's expectations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它肯定达到了、甚至超越了美国转折点组织的预期。

sentences.en: I mean, they got a football stadium for this with a seating capacity of 63,000 and an overflow stadium, I think, that holds another 12,000 or so.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们为此租下了一座容量为63,000人的足球场，还有一个大约能容纳12,000人的溢出体育场。

sentences.en: And both were definitely filled.
sentences.zh: 而且两座体育场绝对都坐满了。

sentences.en: People were turned away.
sentences.zh: 还有人被拒之门外。

sentences.en: And, of course, it was Republican royalty who attended, not only the people on Air Force One and Air Force Two,
sentences.zh: 当然，出席的都是共和党王室成员，不仅有空军一号和空军二号上的人，

sentences.en: but a number of members of Congress and senators as well as cabinet members.
sentences.zh: 还有许多国会议员、参议员以及内阁成员。

sentences.en: That's actually the reason why we wanted to talk to you about what happened today, because, yes, on its face, this was a memorial, of course, but it wasn't just a memorial, right?
sentences.zh: 这其实就是我们想和你聊聊今天所发生事情的原因，因为，是的，表面上看，这是一场追悼会，但它不仅仅是一场追悼会，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it seemed to actually be these two things at once, this service for Charlie Kirk, but also a major political event.
sentences.zh: 因为它似乎同时具有两重属性，既是为查理·柯克举行的追悼仪式，也是一场重大的政治活动。

sentences.en: You had some of the most influential leaders of the MAGA movement at this ceremony.
sentences.zh: 出席这场典礼的有MAGA运动中最具影响力的领导人。

sentences.en: You had the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 你有美国总统。

sentences.en: You had right-wing influencers.
sentences.zh: 你有右翼网红。

sentences.en: All of these people got up and spoke about Charlie Kirk, and underlying all their speeches was this sort of existential message about what his death means for the MAGA movement,
sentences.zh: 所有这些人都起立发言谈论查理·柯克，他们所有演讲的底层逻辑都是一种关于他的死对MAGA运动意味着什么的生存之问，

sentences.en: where it goes from here, and what kind of rallying cry, frankly, different people were hearing in this moment in Charlie Kirk's name.
sentences.zh: 它将走向何方，坦白说，不同的人在此刻以查理·柯克之名听到了什么样的集结号。

sentences.en: And that's what feels like it's important to unpack with you now.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么现在觉得有必要和你一起剖析这一点。

sentences.en: No, I think that's right, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 不，我想你是对的，瑞秋。

sentences.en: I mean, for one thing, start with the fact that Charlie Kirk was the head of this very powerful political organizing force called Turning Point USA.
sentences.zh: 我是说，首先，从查理·柯克是这个名为“美国转折点”的强大政治组织负责人开始说起。

sentences.en: And so to attend a funeral celebrating the life of Charlie Kirk was going to inescapably be a political event.
sentences.zh: 因此，参加一场庆祝查理·柯克生平的葬礼，不可避免地会是一场政治活动。

sentences.en: And so it was.
sentences.zh: 事实也的确如此。

sentences.en: And not only in terms of the fact that a lot of politicians spoke, but because Kirk himself and his death have a lot of portent for the conservative movement.
sentences.zh: 不仅因为许多政治人物发表了讲话，还因为柯克本人以及他的死对保守派运动具有许多预示意义。

sentences.en: And I think that on the heels of his death, we're likely to see a lot of jostling for how to reshape the MAGA movement and in whose image it will be shaped.
sentences.zh: 我认为在他死后，我们很可能会看到围绕如何重塑MAGA运动以及将按照谁的形象重塑而展开的大量争夺。

sentences.en: And in fact, you could see at the event,
sentences.zh: 事实上，你可以在活动中看到，

sentences.en: these two forces of a celebration in the evangelical Christian way of a Christian leader's life collide with the sort of hard knuckle politics of the conservative movement.
sentences.zh: 福音派基督教纪念一位基督教领袖一生的庆祝方式，与保守派运动硬核政治的这两种力量发生了碰撞。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about how those two forces really revealed themselves throughout the course of what was an hours long ceremony.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们来谈谈这两种力量如何在历时数小时的典礼过程中真正显现出来。

sentences.en: How did the memorial actually begin?
sentences.zh: 追悼会到底是如何开始的？

sentences.en: It really bore the stamp of Charlie Kirk's Turning Point USA events, which really had become, over the years, practically rock concerts.
sentences.zh: 它确实带有查理·柯克的“美国转折点”活动的烙印，这些活动多年来实际上已经变得跟摇滚音乐会差不多。

sentences.en: This was more toned down, but still there was this procession of bagpipes playing Amazing Grace.
sentences.zh: 这场虽然低调了一些，但仍然有演奏《奇异恩典》的风笛队游行。

sentences.en: There were two or three famous Christian rock bands playing.
sentences.zh: 有两三支著名的基督教摇滚乐队在演奏。

sentences.en: And so it very much began with all of the tonality of what you'd expect of a funeral at an evangelical megachurch.
sentences.zh: 因此，它的开场非常具有你在福音派巨型教堂葬礼上所期望的所有基调。

sentences.en: That was the atmosphere set by Turning Point, and that's how this funeral began, with speaker after speaker talking about Charlie Kirk's faith.
sentences.zh: 那是“转折点”设定的氛围，这场葬礼也就是这样开始的，一位又一位演讲者谈论着查理·柯克的信仰。

sentences.en: Charlie Kirk called me his pastor.
sentences.zh: 查理·柯克叫我他的牧师。

sentences.en: I called him my friend.
sentences.zh: 我叫他我的朋友。

sentences.en: He loved God more than he loved safety or applause or even his own life.
sentences.zh: 他爱上帝胜过爱安全、掌声甚至他自己的生命。

sentences.en: The legacy he built, his values, his love of God, and true joy he found in his Savior, Jesus ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 他建立的传承、他的价值观、他对上帝的爱，以及他在救世主耶稣基督身上找到的真正的喜乐。

sentences.en: And how that not only anchored him, but inspired so many people.
sentences.zh: 以及这不仅如何支撑了他，还激励了如此多的人。

sentences.en: And so there was a period composed purely of speeches given by people who had worked with Kirk.
sentences.zh: 因此有一段时间纯粹是由与柯克共事过的人发表的演讲组成。

sentences.en: It was the honor of my life to serve you as you serve Jesus.
sentences.zh: 在我侍奉耶稣的同时能够服务你，是我一生的荣幸。

sentences.en: There was no discussion of partisan politics.
sentences.zh: 其中没有任何关于党派政治的讨论。

sentences.en: And I would say this to all of you, the Lord loves you.
sentences.zh: 我要对在座的各位说，主爱你们。

sentences.en: And it's notable that in that first hour, there were no elected officials on stage.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，在第一个小时里，台上没有民选官员。

sentences.en: You see, Charlie looked at politics as an on-ramp to Jesus.
sentences.zh: 你看，查理把政治视为通往耶稣的引桥。

sentences.en: He knew if he could get all of you rowing in the streams of liberty, you'd come to its source, and that's the Lord.
sentences.zh: 他知道如果他能让你们所有人在自由的溪流中齐心协力，你们就会找到它的源头，那就是主。

sentences.en: Robert, you alluded to the fact that that wasn't the case all day.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，你刚才暗示说，一整天并非一直如此。

sentences.en: Can you just help describe when does the tone start to change?
sentences.zh: 你能帮忙描述一下基调是从什么时候开始改变的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Roughly around midway, the biographical picture of Charlie Kirk as a father, a husband, a leader, and an inspiration begins to move.
sentences.zh: 大约在进行到一半时，查理·柯克作为父亲、丈夫、领袖和灵感源泉的传记形象开始转变。

sentences.en: And replacing it is the notion of Charlie Kirk martyr.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是查理·柯克烈士的概念。

sentences.en: 11 days ago, my friend was martyred for using his voice to engage in peaceful dialogue.
sentences.zh: 11天前，我的朋友因为用他的声音进行和平对话而殉道。

sentences.en: Charlie Kirk, a Christian warrior who was felled by the left.
sentences.zh: 查理·柯克，一位被左翼击倒的基督教勇士。

sentences.en: And it's easy to note that the more political figures take the stage, the more you see that language get ratcheted up.
sentences.zh: 不难发现，政治人物上台越多，你就会看到这种语言升级得越厉害。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, please welcome Benny Johnson.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，请欢迎本尼·约翰逊。

sentences.en: The first that really stood out to me was by the right-wing podcaster, Benny Johnson.
sentences.zh: 对我而言真正脱颖而出的是右翼播客本尼·约翰逊的发言。

sentences.en: Fight for Charlie Kirk!
sentences.zh: 为查理·柯克而战！

sentences.en: Who feels the Holy Spirit in the house tonight?
sentences.zh: 今晚谁在这个大厅里感受到了圣灵？

sentences.en: Who had done a lot of Turning Point USA events, was really a lieutenant in a way of Kirk's.
sentences.zh: 他举办过很多“美国转折点”的活动，在某种程度上确实是柯克的心腹。

sentences.en: They were very close.
sentences.zh: 他们非常亲密。

sentences.en: And his speech was the first one, I believe, that talked about the mission against evil.
sentences.zh: 我相信他的演讲是第一个谈到抗击邪恶使命的演讲。

sentences.en: And so we want to thank the administration for being here and carrying out that godly mission of wielding the sword against evil.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要感谢政府来到这里，并执行挥舞利剑抗击邪恶的神圣使命。

sentences.en: And that's an exact phrase that he used about wielding the sword in that godly mission against evil.
sentences.zh: 这正是他所使用的原话，关于在反对邪恶的神圣使命中挥舞利剑。

sentences.en: Please welcome to the stage, Jack Posobiec.
sentences.zh: 请杰克·波索比奇上台。

sentences.en: Shortly after him came Jack Posobiec.
sentences.zh: 紧随他之后的是杰克·波索比奇。

sentences.en: Charlie Kirk was my friend.
sentences.zh: 查理·柯克是我的朋友。

sentences.en: Charlie was my brother.
sentences.zh: 查理是我的兄弟。

sentences.en: And Charlie was my commanding officer.
sentences.zh: 而查理是我的指挥官。

sentences.en: Another close friend of Charlie Kirk's and another podcaster who compared Kirk to Moses at the top of the mountain.
sentences.zh: 查理·柯克的另一位挚友、也是另一位播客，他将柯克比作山顶上的摩西。

sentences.en: The Bible tells us that on his last day, Moses looked across the River Jordan and he saw the promised land.
sentences.zh: 圣经告诉我们，在他生命的最后一天，摩西眺望约旦河对岸，看到了应许之地。

sentences.en: He led the people there, but he did not cross himself.
sentences.zh: 他带领人民到了那里，但自己并没有过河。

sentences.en: And said that though Charlie Kirk may not have gotten to the promised land, he has brought us all there to the promised land.
sentences.zh: 并表示尽管查理·柯克可能没有到达应许之地，但他把我们所有人都带到了那里，带到了应许之地。

sentences.en: On his last day, Charlie Kirk led us there.
sentences.zh: 在他生命的最后一天，查理·柯克带领我们到了那里。

sentences.en: And Charlie Kirk has brought us to the promised land.
sentences.zh: 而查理·柯克把我们带到了应许之地。

sentences.en: But he was saying that...
sentences.zh: 但他当时在说的是……

sentences.en: And the question of our time, will Western civilization endure?
sentences.zh: 我们这个时代的问题是，西方文明会延续下去吗？

sentences.en: You know, that the sacrifice of Charles James Kirk will be seen a century from now as the turning point of civilization.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，查尔斯·詹姆斯·柯克的牺牲在一个世纪后将被视为文明的转折点。

sentences.en: That a century from now, when they write of the two or three pivotal moments that led to the saving of Western civilization,
sentences.zh: 一个世纪后，当人们书写引领拯救西方文明的两三个关键时刻时，

sentences.en: they will write that the sacrifice of Charles James Kirk was the turning point.
sentences.zh: 他们会写道，查尔斯·詹姆斯·柯克的牺牲就是那个转折点。

sentences.en: And that Western civilization was saved by Charlie Kirk.
sentences.zh: 而西方文明是被查理·柯克拯救的。

sentences.en: He talked about fighting evil in the highest of places.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了在至高处与邪恶战斗。

sentences.en: For Charlie, we will end the evil disease that split us and took Charlie from us.
sentences.zh: 为了查理，我们将结束分裂我们并夺走查理的邪恶疾病。

sentences.en: And for Charlie, turning point USA will last forever.
sentences.zh: 为了查理，美国转折点将永远持续下去。

sentences.en: So those two really, I think, set the tone for the political speeches that were to follow.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这两个人真正为接下来的政治演讲定下了基调。

sentences.en: We were also, by the way, I should say, we were watching along here in the New York Times office.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，应该说，我们当时也在《纽约时报》办公室里一起观看。

sentences.en: And that's what really struck me, was that part of the messaging seemed to be this positioning of Kirk as part of this larger divine plan.
sentences.zh: 真正让我震惊的是，传达的信息的一部分似乎是将柯克定位为更宏大的神圣计划的一部分。

sentences.en: And in so doing that, the point was also to position the larger MAGA movement within that same divine plan,
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，其目的也是将更大的MAGA运动定位在同一个神圣计划中，

sentences.en: to basically say this is something that is, like, handed down by the will of God in a way that was a little bit, frankly,
sentences.zh: 基本上是说这是某种由上帝意志赋予的事情，坦白说，这有点

sentences.en: reminiscent of the assassination attempt of Donald Trump, where we saw just days later at the Republican National Convention,
sentences.zh: 让人想起唐纳德·特朗普的暗杀未遂事件，我们在几天后的共和党全国代表大会上就看到了这一点

sentences.en: there was this really revealing statement that basically Trump was saved by God to save the country.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常发人深省的说法，大意是上帝拯救特朗普是为了拯救这个国家。

sentences.en: So it all felt of a piece in a way.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切在某种程度上都感觉是一个整体。

sentences.en: Yes, and I think that this was reminiscent, because in both cases, the third person, plural, was frequently invoked by the right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这让人回想起来，因为在这两种情况下，右翼都经常使用第一人称复数“我们”……不对，这里用的是第三人称复数“他们”。

sentences.en: They tried to do this to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们试图对特朗普总统这样做。

sentences.en: They did this to Charlie Kirk.
sentences.zh: 他们对查理·柯克做了这件事。

sentences.en: They also had a goal of gaining control of the media and Hollywood so they could change the culture in America.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标还包括控制媒体和好莱坞，以便他们能够改变美国的文化。

sentences.en: They kill and terrorize their opponents, hoping to silence them.
sentences.zh: 他们杀害并恐吓对手，希望能让他们闭嘴。

sentences.en: Who do you think they were talking about when they said that evil they?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们在说那个邪恶的“他们”时指的是谁？

sentences.en: It's pretty vague, though those individuals who were saying they had in the past meant the left when they were referring to they.
sentences.zh: 这相当含糊，不过过去说出“他们”的那些人，在指代“他们”时指的是左翼。

sentences.en: But it ceases to be an inference and becomes abundantly clear who they is once Donald Trump Jr.
sentences.zh: 但一旦小唐纳德·特朗普登上舞台，

sentences.en: took the stage.
sentences.zh: 这就不再是一种推断，而是变得极其清晰——“他们”到底是谁。

sentences.en: The true extremists are those who would justify and celebrate taking an innocent life over nothing more than disagreement.
sentences.zh: 真正的极端分子是那些仅仅因为意见不合，就为夺走无辜生命辩护并进行庆祝的人。

sentences.en: That is the real radicalism.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正的激进主义。

sentences.en: Jr.
sentences.zh: 小特朗普

sentences.en: was the first person on the stage to use the phrase fake news media or even to talk about liberals on campus going crazy.
sentences.zh: 是舞台上第一个使用“假新闻媒体”这个词，甚至谈到校园自由派发疯的人。

sentences.en: Because the left-wing activists, they were going crazy.
sentences.zh: 因为左翼激进分子，他们当时正在发疯。

sentences.en: And actually was also the first person to mention any Democrat at all when...
sentences.zh: 事实上，他也是第一个在讲话中提到任何民主党人的人……

sentences.en: To say Charlie knew more about the Bible than me is an understatement, folks.
sentences.zh: 说查理比我更懂圣经，这可真是太谦虚了，诸位。

sentences.en: Don Jr.
sentences.zh: 小唐纳德·特朗普

sentences.en: trying to kind of crack a joke about how little he knows about the Bible said, obviously, that's an understatement.
sentences.zh: 试图开个玩笑，调侃自己对圣经知之甚少，他显然说这太谦虚了。

sentences.en: It's like saying Donald Trump knows more about being president than Hillary Clinton or Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 这就好比说唐纳德·特朗普比希拉里·克林顿或卡玛拉·哈里斯更懂得如何当总统。

sentences.en: No kidding!
sentences.zh: 可不是嘛！

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That was the moment where it seemed like it went from a memorial to an overtly political moment.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，感觉就像是从一场追悼会变成了一个公开的政治时刻。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: And especially when we hear Don Jr.
sentences.zh: 特别是当我们听到小唐纳德·特朗普

sentences.en: close his remarks the way he did, because he kind of did this repetition of saying, you know, if you believe in God and country...
sentences.zh: 像那样结束他的发言时，因为他重复了一句类似的话，你知道的，如果你信仰上帝和国家……

sentences.en: If you believe in God and family and country, you are one of us.
sentences.zh: 如果你信仰上帝、家庭和国家，你就是我们的一员。

sentences.en: You are one of us, of course, implying that if you don't believe in God and country, you're not one of us.
sentences.zh: 你就是我们的一员，当然，这也暗示着如果你不信仰上帝和国家，你就不是我们的一员。

sentences.en: If you reject the propaganda of the fake news media, welcome!
sentences.zh: 如果你拒绝假新闻媒体的宣传，欢迎加入！

sentences.en: So he establishes kind of the MAGA set of grievances or the MAGA set of virtues and then basically says, use Charlie Kirk's death to come closer into our movement.
sentences.zh: 因此，他确立了一套MAGA（让美国再次伟大）的委屈或MAGA的美德，然后基本上说，利用查理·柯克的死来更紧密地融入我们的运动。

sentences.en: Charlie loved this country, its people, and the work of persuading others to believe in something greater than themselves.
sentences.zh: 查理热爱这个国家、这里的人民，以及劝说他人相信比自身更伟大的事业的工作。

sentences.en: At this point in the memorial, it really sort of felt as though the messaging that was coming through was Charlie Kirk was a prophet.
sentences.zh: 在追悼会的这个阶段，人们确实有一种感觉，那就是传达出的信息是：查理·柯克是一位先知。

sentences.en: He died for you in the audience for this movement.
sentences.zh: 他是为了在座的你们、为了这场运动而死的。

sentences.en: And therefore, you should join us in our fight against the evil them, whatever that fight might look like.
sentences.zh: 因此，无论这场斗争看起来是什么样的，你们都应该加入我们，共同对抗那个邪恶的“他们”。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: And I think that the next speaker, Vice President J.D.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为接下来的发言者，副总统J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, made that message even more explicit when he said to the audience that, to use Vance's words, that Charlie Kirk was murdered for speaking the truth.
sentences.zh: 万斯，用万斯的话说，他告诉台下观众，查理·柯克是因为说真话而被谋杀的，这让这一信息更加明确。

sentences.en: Because he was murdered for speaking the truth.
sentences.zh: 因为他是因为说真话而被谋杀的。

sentences.en: And that evil is among us.
sentences.zh: 而这种邪恶就在我们身边。

sentences.en: I think he would encourage me to be honest, that evil still walks among us.
sentences.zh: 我想他会鼓励我诚实地说，邪恶依然在我们身边游荡。

sentences.en: Not to ignore it for the sake of a fake kumbaya moment, but to address it head on and honestly as the sickness that it is.
sentences.zh: 不要为了虚假的融洽时刻而忽视它，而是要像面对一种疾病那样，正面而诚实地去解决它。

sentences.en: This is not going to be a kumbaya moment, you know, one where we all just kind of come together.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个大团圆的时刻，你知道的，不是那种我们所有人欢聚一堂的时刻。

sentences.en: So the movement there is not just one of carrying on bigger and better than before, but to defeat the evil that indeed tried to defeat Charlie Kirk.
sentences.zh: 所以那里的运动不仅仅是比以往更大、更好、继续前进，而是要战胜那些确实试图打败查理·柯克的邪恶。

sentences.en: Which, if you just pause for a second, seems like a really stunning thing to hear from the Vice President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 如果你停顿一秒钟想一想，从美国副总统口中听到这样的话似乎是一件极其震撼的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, one way to look at what he is saying here from a more cynical viewpoint, if you're thinking that this is really being seized on as a political moment,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你从一个更冷嘲热讽的角度来看他在这里所说的话，如果你认为这确实被当作了一个政治时刻来利用的话，

sentences.en: is that by saying basically join us in our fight against them, in a way,
sentences.zh: 那就是通过说基本上加入我们对抗他们的斗争中，在某种程度上，

sentences.en: it's like laying the groundwork for justification of whatever actions might be taken to strike back against this enemy on the left, right?
sentences.zh: 这就好象是在为反击左翼这个敌人的任何可能采取的行动提供正当性铺平道路，对吧？

sentences.en: Even if those actions aren't super clear in this moment?
sentences.zh: 即使这些行动在目前还不是超级清晰？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I think that's been a subtext of the MAGA movement, at least since 2020, when Trump ran for re-election for the first time, that the left is incorrigible,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是MAGA运动的潜台词，至少自2020年特朗普首次竞选连任以来一直是这样，即左翼是无可救药的，

sentences.en: the left cannot be persuaded.
sentences.zh: 左翼是无法被说服的。

sentences.en: It's not anything new, but it has become much more intense and the language, I think, much more stark.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么新鲜事，但它变得更加强烈了，而且我认为语言也更加严厉。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's one thing to hear, you know, a broadcaster say it.
sentences.zh: 当然，听到某个广播员这么说是一回事，

sentences.en: Another thing entirely, to hear the Vice President of the United States say it from his position of stature.
sentences.zh: 听到美国副总统从他的崇高地位说出这话完全是另一回事。

sentences.en: As I was watching throughout the night, it really felt like there was a kind of wavering between these two messages that you have described to us.
sentences.zh: 当我在整个晚上观看时，真的感觉在给我们描述的这两种信息之间存在某种摇摆。

sentences.en: This religious message, and then a more political and pugilistic message.
sentences.zh: 这种宗教信息，以及随之而来的更加政治化和好战的信息。

sentences.en: And at times, these really seem to be overlapping with some of these speakers.
sentences.zh: 有时，这些信息在某些发言者身上似乎确实重叠了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And as it turned out, and I think this was entirely unintentional, but completely remarkable to see, the final two speakers of the evening would represent,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我想这完全是无意中发生的，但看到这一幕完全非同寻常，当晚的最后两位发言者将代表，

sentences.en: in diametric opposition to each other, those two very viewpoints.
sentences.zh: 以截然相反的方式，代表这两种截然不同的观点。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wenna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是韦娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”（Connections）游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的一个谜题，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都创作“拼写蜜蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母箱”（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游玩。

sentences.en: So, Robert, take us to the end of the memorial and the final two speakers.
sentences.zh: 那么，罗伯特，带我们了解追悼会的尾声和最后两位发言者。

sentences.en: Tell us who they were and what they said.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们他们是谁，说了些什么。

sentences.en: Please give a warm welcome to Mrs. Erica Kirk.
sentences.zh: 请热烈欢迎埃里卡·柯克女士。

sentences.en: The penultimate speaker was Erica Kirk, the wife of Charlie Kirk, and now the CEO and chair of Turning Point USA.
sentences.zh: 倒数第二位发言者是埃里卡·柯克，查理·柯克的妻子，现在是美国转折点组织（Turning Point USA）的首席执行官兼主席。

sentences.en: God bless all of you for coming here from all over the world to honor and celebrate my Charlie.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑你们所有从世界各地赶来这里悼念和颂扬我的查理的人。

sentences.en: It was, in many ways, the representation of the spiritual side, not only of Turning Point USA and not only of Charlie Kirk,
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这代表了精神层面，不仅是美国转折点组织和查理·柯克的精神，

sentences.en: but of how those closest to Kirk wanted to view his death.
sentences.zh: 也是柯克最亲近的人希望如何看待他的死。

sentences.en: Eleven days ago, God accepted that total surrender from my husband and then called him to his side.
sentences.zh: 十一天前，上帝接受了我丈夫的全然顺服，然后将他召至身侧。

sentences.en: She spoke very declaratively about not only her husband and what their marriage was like.
sentences.zh: 她非常坚定地谈到了她的丈夫以及他们的婚姻生活是什么样的。

sentences.en: Charlie perfectly understood God's role for a Christian husband.
sentences.zh: 查理完全理解上帝对一个基督教丈夫的角色设定。

sentences.en: But also, it was an interesting evocation of what she believed a conservative Christian marriage should look like and what it should not look like.
sentences.zh: 但同时，这也是对她所认为的保守派基督教婚姻应该是什么样、不应该是什么样的一种有趣的唤起。

sentences.en: But please be a leader worth following.
sentences.zh: 但是请做一个值得追随的领袖。

sentences.en: Your wife is not your servant.
sentences.zh: 你的妻子不是你的仆人。

sentences.en: There was a point where she said, your wife is not your servant.
sentences.zh: 有一个节点她说，你的妻子不是你的仆人。

sentences.en: Your wife is not your employee.
sentences.zh: 你的妻子不是你的雇员。

sentences.en: Your wife is not your slave.
sentences.zh: 你的妻子不是你的奴隶。

sentences.en: But your wife is your helper, I believe she said.
sentences.zh: 但我相信她说过，你的妻子是你的帮手。

sentences.en: She is your helper.
sentences.zh: 她是你的帮手。

sentences.en: Is your helper, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是你的帮手，没错。

sentences.en: You are one flesh working together for the glory of God.
sentences.zh: 你们是一体，为了上帝的荣耀共同努力。

sentences.en: And so, what she was describing was, in a much, much softer way, what a conservative Christian union would look like.
sentences.zh: 因此，她所描述的是以一种温和得多得多的方式，描绘了一个保守的基督教结合会是什么样子。

sentences.en: Charlie passionately wanted to reach and save the lost boys of the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 查理热切地想要接触并拯救西方迷失的男孩们。

sentences.en: The young men who feel like they have no direction.
sentences.zh: 那些觉得自己没有方向的年轻人们。

sentences.en: But I'd say that, easily the most memorable thing that Erica Kirk said.
sentences.zh: 但我要说的是，埃里卡·柯克所说的话中，最令人难忘的毫无疑问是

sentences.en: He wanted to save young men, just like the one who took his life.
sentences.zh: 他想要拯救年轻人，就像夺走他生命的那个年轻人一样。

sentences.en: Were three words.
sentences.zh: 这三个字。

sentences.en: I forgive him.
sentences.zh: 我原谅他。

sentences.en: I forgive him.
sentences.zh: 我原谅他。

sentences.en: Referring to the alleged murderer.
sentences.zh: 指的是涉嫌谋杀的人。

sentences.en: And she got a standing ovation and wept as everyone clapped.
sentences.zh: 她赢得了全场起立鼓掌，在所有人的掌声中落泪。

sentences.en: I forgive him because it was what Christ did.
sentences.zh: 我原谅他，因为这是基督所做的事。

sentences.en: And it's what Charlie would do.
sentences.zh: 这也是查理会做的事。

sentences.en: She was speaking the language of non-violent politics.
sentences.zh: 她说的非暴力政治的语言。

sentences.en: Where others were talking about how her husband had been silenced.
sentences.zh: 当其他人都在谈论她的丈夫是如何被剥夺话语权时，

sentences.en: Her framing of that was, when you stop the dialogue, then violence comes into the scene.
sentences.zh: 她的框架是，当你停止对话时，暴力就会粉墨登场。

sentences.en: The answer to hate is not hate.
sentences.zh: 仇恨的答案不是仇恨。

sentences.en: The answer we know from the gospel is love and always love.
sentences.zh: 我们从福音中知道，答案是爱，永远是爱。

sentences.en: Love for our enemies.
sentences.zh: 爱我们的敌人。

sentences.en: And love for those who persecute us.
sentences.zh: 爱那些迫害我们的人。

sentences.en: Had the program concluded after Erica Kirk, it would have felt like an entirely different thing.
sentences.zh: 如果节目在埃里卡·柯克发言后结束，感觉将会完全不同。

sentences.en: That's not, of course, what took place.
sentences.zh: 当然，事情并非如此。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you very much, Lee.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你，李。

sentences.en: The other main event was the President of the United States, Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 另一个重头戏是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And maybe 10 to 15 minutes into his speech, Donald Trump, as he is wont to do, said the quiet part out loud.
sentences.zh: 也许在他演讲进行了10到15分钟时，唐纳德·特朗普像他惯常做的那样，把本该隐晦的话大声地讲了出来。

sentences.en: The left, the left, I call it the radical left.
sentences.zh: 左翼，左翼，我称之为激进左翼。

sentences.en: I call it sometimes the radical left lunatics.
sentences.zh: 我有时称之为激进左翼狂热分子。

sentences.en: It gave a name to who the they was, who it was that was silencing Charlie Kirk, who was the enemy.
sentences.zh: 这给“他们”指名道姓了，明确了究竟是谁在让查理·柯克闭嘴，谁是敌人。

sentences.en: He called them the radical left lunatics.
sentences.zh: 他称他们为激进左翼狂热分子。

sentences.en: And then Trump interrupted himself and said...
sentences.zh: 然后特朗普打断了自己并说道……

sentences.en: But Charlie didn't say that.
sentences.zh: 但查理可没这么说。

sentences.en: He called it the left.
sentences.zh: 他称之为左翼。

sentences.en: But Charlie didn't say that.
sentences.zh: 但查理没这么说。

sentences.en: He just called them the left.
sentences.zh: 他只是称他们为左翼。

sentences.en: And then, as an aside...
sentences.zh: 然后，作为题外话……

sentences.en: He was probably right, but I can't help it.
sentences.zh: 他可能是对的，但我实在忍不住。

sentences.en: I can't help it.
sentences.zh: 我忍不住。

sentences.en: The President went on and said, he was probably right, but I couldn't help myself.
sentences.zh: 总统继续说道，他可能是对的，但我情不自禁。

sentences.en: And so, by Trump comparing himself to Charlie Kirk there, he was, in this interesting way,
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普在那里将自己与查理·柯克进行比较时，他以这种有趣的方式，

sentences.en: making Charlie kind of the diplomatic political type and making himself the outsider and truth teller.
sentences.zh: 把查理塑造成外交政治型人物，而把自己塑造成局外人和说真话的人。

sentences.en: He did not hate his opponents.
sentences.zh: 他没有仇恨他的对手。

sentences.en: He wanted the best for them.
sentences.zh: 他希望他们有最好的结果。

sentences.en: That's where I disagreed with Charlie.
sentences.zh: 这就是我与查理意见相左的地方。

sentences.en: Charlie, I hate my opponent.
sentences.zh: 查理，我恨我的对手。

sentences.en: And I don't want the best for them.
sentences.zh: 我不想让他们有最好的结果。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: I am sorry, Erica.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉，埃里卡。

sentences.en: He was establishing permission for everyone in the audience to basically hate your enemy, to want the worst for them, to really want to smite them.
sentences.zh: 他是在为台下的每一个人树立准许：基本上可以恨你的敌人，希望他们倒霉，真心想要痛击他们。

sentences.en: And then Trump took it a step further and basically said that he had warned Charlie Kirk about going to these campus events.
sentences.zh: 然后特朗普更进一步，基本上说他曾警告过查理·柯克不要去参加这些校园活动。

sentences.en: There were bomb threats, pulled fire alarms, and countless rage-filled radicals who tried to shout him down.
sentences.zh: 那里有炸弹威胁、拉响的火警警报，以及无数充满愤怒的激进分子试图大声喧哗压倒他。

sentences.en: It was nasty.
sentences.zh: 这太恶劣了。

sentences.en: I used to say, Charlie, this is nasty stuff you're doing.
sentences.zh: 我过去常说，查理，你做的事太恶劣了。

sentences.en: He thought it was great on the one hand, but he also said, Charlie, this is nasty stuff you're doing.
sentences.zh: 一方面他认为这很棒，但他也说过，查理，你做的事太恶劣了。

sentences.en: And so he certainly wasn't blaming Kirk for his own assassination, but he was saying, I warned you this kind of thing would happen.
sentences.zh: 所以他当然不是在责怪柯克招致了暗杀，但他是在说，我警告过你这种事会发生。

sentences.en: These are the kind of people we're dealing with.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们正在打交道的那类人。

sentences.en: And the violence comes largely from the left.
sentences.zh: 暴力很大程度上来自左翼。

sentences.en: You don't hear that from too many people, do you?
sentences.zh: 你没从太多人那里听到过这话，对吧？

sentences.en: In the end, these people can't be reasoned with.
sentences.zh: 到头来，这些人是无法与之讲道理的。

sentences.en: You just have to kind of steamroller them.
sentences.zh: 你只能把他们给强行平推过去。

sentences.en: God bless the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑美利坚合众国。

sentences.en: And could I ask Erica, please come out.
sentences.zh: 我能请埃里卡上来吗？

sentences.en: Erica, please come out.
sentences.zh: 埃里卡，请出来吧。

sentences.en: It felt like compared to Erica Kirk's speech, ultimately, these are two very different views of where this movement that Kirk started is supposed to go from here.
sentences.zh: 感觉与埃里卡·柯克的演讲相比，归根结底，对于柯克发起的这场运动接下来该走向何方，这是两种截然不同的观点。

sentences.en: And you're getting these two different views from arguably the two most important speakers at this event.
sentences.zh: 而且这两种不同的观点可以说来自于这场活动中最至关重要的两位发言者。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Erica has not spoken much at all about her own political views beyond the fact that she supports Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 除了支持唐纳德·特朗普之外，埃里卡几乎没有怎么谈论过她自己的政治观点。

sentences.en: She's not as politically explicit as her husband is.
sentences.zh: 她不像她丈夫那样在政治上那么直白。

sentences.en: But, you know, while I was listening to Trump give his tribute to Charlie Kirk, I did find myself thinking from time to time, you know,
sentences.zh: 不过呢，当我在听特朗普对查理·柯克表达敬意时，我确实发现自己时不时地在想，你知道的，

sentences.en: this is not – it may be cognitively dissonant with Erica Kirk, who we just heard.
sentences.zh: 这并不是——它可能与我们刚刚听到的埃里卡·柯克存在认知失调。

sentences.en: But it's not necessarily cognitively dissonant with Charlie Kirk.
sentences.zh: 但这未必与查理·柯克存在认知失调。

sentences.en: And I began thinking about that, particularly when Trump talked about his beautiful victories.
sentences.zh: 我开始思考这个问题，尤其是当特朗普谈到他那些漂亮的胜选时。

sentences.en: And then he actually talked about 2020.
sentences.zh: 然后他真的谈到了2020年。

sentences.en: And he said, we really did great that night, too.
sentences.zh: 他说，那天晚上我们确实也干得非常棒。

sentences.en: He said, but they cheated like dogs.
sentences.zh: 他说，但他们像狗一样作弊。

sentences.en: But we got them back, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 不过我们回敬了他们，对吧？

sentences.en: And the reason I was thinking of that was that Charlie Kirk was one of the most prominent voices in saying that the election was rigged.
sentences.zh: 我之所以会这么想，是因为查理·柯克曾是声称选举被操纵的最著名的声音之一。

sentences.en: And he never took back those words.
sentences.zh: 而他从未收回过那些言论。

sentences.en: So, it was interesting then to listen to the speech and hear how he framed Charlie Kirk as the kind of more diplomatic between himself and Kirk.
sentences.zh: 所以，听取这个演讲并听他如何将查理·柯克塑造成他与柯克之间更具外交风范的那个人，这就很有意思了。

sentences.en: That, in fact, Kirk's belief system did not depart that greatly from Trump's.
sentences.zh: 事实上，柯克的信仰体系与特朗普并没有太大的出入。

sentences.en: He also believed that the border should be sealed.
sentences.zh: 他也认为应该封锁边境。

sentences.en: In fact, Kirk, in his final year or so, was really talking about how even legal immigration must cease.
sentences.zh: 事实上，柯克在大约最后一年里，一直在谈论甚至连合法移民也必须停止。

sentences.en: He has talked about transgender individuals as being mentally ill, Kirk has, which is very much consonant with what Trump has said.
sentences.zh: 柯克曾把跨性别者称为精神病人，这与特朗普所说的话非常一致。

sentences.en: You're saying that there wasn't a lot of daylight between these two men.
sentences.zh: 你是说这两个男人之间其实没有什么根本分歧。

sentences.en: No, there was a great deal of daylight in how they couched things.
sentences.zh: 不，他们在措辞的表述上有很大的分歧。

sentences.en: But in terms of hardcore policy beliefs, these guys were pretty much in lockstep.
sentences.zh: 但在核心政策信仰方面，这些人可以说是高度一致。

sentences.en: But obviously now his wife has taken over the institution that he started.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，现在他的妻子接管了他创立的机构。

sentences.en: And her message was just so starkly different than some of the political rallying cries that we heard.
sentences.zh: 而她的信息与我们听到的一些政治集会口号截然不同。

sentences.en: And so I just wonder which one of these messages you think is going to win out at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想知道，你认为终究会是哪一种信息胜出。

sentences.en: Because in some ways they seem to be in tension or in conflict.
sentences.zh: 因为在某些方面，它们似乎处于紧张或冲突之中。

sentences.en: I agree with you because I think that Erica Kirk views herself, if she views herself in any kind of large capacity, as a spiritual leader.
sentences.zh: 我同意你的看法，因为我认为埃里卡·柯克如果认为自己有什么大作为的话，她将自己视为精神领袖。

sentences.en: Where Charlie Kirk was a spiritual person who was a political leader, Turning Point USA was a fusion of those two.
sentences.zh: 如果说查理·柯克是一个具有政治领袖身份的精神人物，那么美国转折点组织就是这两者的融合。

sentences.en: So will the new CEO, the new chair, Erica Kirk, become more politically overt when she goes to visit campuses, as her husband did, and as she pledged to do in her speech,
sentences.zh: 那么新的首席执行官、新主席埃里卡·柯克，在她去访问大学时，会像她丈夫以前那样，也像她在演讲中所承诺的那样，变得更加公开涉足政治吗，

sentences.en: will she go just to meet and give speeches?
sentences.zh: 她去只是为了会面和发表演讲吗？

sentences.en: Or is she going to engage in the kind of rigorous give-and-take debate that Charlie Kirk did?
sentences.zh: 还是说她会参与查理·柯克那种严格的针锋相对的辩论？

sentences.en: Will she be giving campaign speeches?
sentences.zh: 她会发表竞选演讲吗？

sentences.en: It's really hard to know, like, what if any role a person named Kirk will play in American politics now that Charlie Kirk has left the stage for good.
sentences.zh: 现在查理·柯克已经彻底退出了历史舞台，很难知道一个叫柯克的人还会在美国政治中发挥什么作用（如果有的话）。

sentences.en: Just to step back for a minute, because we just heard a lot of people today say on stage and even some attendees that Kirk's death is the turning point.
sentences.zh: 退一步讲，因为我们今天刚刚听到台上的很多人甚至一些与会者都说，柯克的死是一个转折点。

sentences.en: And I wonder what you make of that.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你对此有何看法。

sentences.en: I'm so glad you asked that, because the phrase turning point now is so fraught with significance, but no one seems to be able to articulate just what that means.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你问这个问题，因为“转折点”这个词现在充满了意义，但似乎没有人能说清楚这到底意味着什么。

sentences.en: There are many people who feel like his assassination marks a kind of turning point that it has to have changed something.
sentences.zh: 许多人觉得他的遇刺标志着某种转折点，它必定改变了某些东西。

sentences.en: I mean, we heard over and over, one thing that really won't change is Turning Point USA, except it'll be bigger and better than before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们一次又一次地听到，有一件事确实不会变，那就是美国转折点组织，只不过它会比以前更大、更好。

sentences.en: But basically, we'll continue Charlie's work.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，我们会继续查理的工作。

sentences.en: But then, what does?
sentences.zh: 然而，接下来会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: We seem at least, you know, and this is not nothing, in the 11 days since Kirk's assassination, there has not been this roiling violence from the right.
sentences.zh: 至少在我们看来——这并非微不足道，在柯克遇刺后的11天里，右翼并没有出现这种汹涌的暴力活动。

sentences.en: But is there going to be an agreement that that is not the way?
sentences.zh: 但大家是否会达成共识，认为那不是正确的道路？

sentences.en: Everyone seems to feel like this was a moment, but what the moment signifies in terms of how it turns our nation, no one's been able to say.
sentences.zh: 每个人似乎都觉得这是一个历史时刻，但这个时刻对于我们国家将如何转向究竟意味着什么，没有人能够说得清。

sentences.en: Robert, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又令人兴奋的权力斗争之中。
